Conrad browse by type volume/amplification amplification treble booster browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Conrad Sky Hawk - Fuzz and Treble Booster Published on September 16, 2012 Conrad fuzz treble boost pedal picture by Todd Ostertag 1968 catalog 1968 catalog Information The Conrad Sky Hawk is a late-1960s fuzz and treble booster pedal designed by Applied Audio Products Inc. of New Jersey and distributed under the Conrad brand by David Wexler & Co. Though no confirmed surviving examples have been documented, the model is listed in period catalogs alongside the Conrad Fuzzy Fury and Bass Hawk, indicating that it was part of the same family of Applied-built effects distributed through Wexler's nationwide dealer network. Based on its placement within the product line and its shared lineage with other Applied Audio designs, the Sky Hawk was almost certainly derived from the Applied Fuzz and Treble Booster circuit used across several OEM-labeled pedals such as those from Crown, Sano, and Lou Rose. These units combined a transistorized fuzz effect with a high-frequency boost, offering two tone-shaping functions that could be used independently or together. The result was a sharp, mid-focused fuzz with an additional treble emphasis suited to cutting through band mixes or accentuating lead tones. Like other Applied Audio pedals of the same period, the Sky Hawk would have featured a compact metal housing, three front-mounted control knobs, and toggle or push switches for effect activation. It was likely powered by a 9V battery and constructed with point-to-point wiring using germanium or early silicon transistors. Catalog listings place it within the later phase of Applied's production, making it a probable transition design between their 1960s fuzz boosters and later multi-effect pedals such as the Guild FW-3.
